Convert duration data to binary

Source: R/utils.R
convert_duration_to_binary.Rd

Converts data on the time dyads spent interacting into approximate binary data, for use with a binary edge model. Both the time spent interacting and the time observed are divided by max_event_length and rounded, so each row records the number of periods of that length with an event, out of the number of periods observed. This is a rough approximation: use it with caution, and make sure all durations are in the same units.

Usage

convert_duration_to_binary(df, event_name, divisor_name, max_event_length)

Arguments

df

Original data frame, ready for use with bison_model().

event_name

Name of the column with the time spent interacting.

divisor_name

Name of the column with the time observed.

max_event_length

The maximum length of time a single social event could last, in the same units as the durations.

Value

The input data frame with the event_name and divisor_name columns replaced by counts suitable for a binary model, with the converted divisor_name column as the effort, e.g. (time_together | time_observed) ~ dyad(node_1, node_2).

See also

bison_model()

Examples

df <- data.frame(
  node_1 = c("A", "A", "B"), node_2 = c("B", "C", "C"),
  time_together = c(30, 0, 10), time_observed = c(60, 60, 60)
)
convert_duration_to_binary(df, "time_together", "time_observed", max_event_length = 10)
#>   node_1 node_2 time_together time_observed
#> 1      A      B             3             6
#> 2      A      C             0             6
#> 3      B      C             1             6
